scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all reach across the
data-center fabric -- pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is unreachable, though pc_0_0
can still ping its own gateway 10.0.0.1. The NOC adds that both
spine routers reported their BGP session toward leaf_router_0_0 going
down at the same moment, while the leaf's uplink interfaces still
show UP. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and watchfrr) on leaf_router_0_0

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 bgpd
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_0 is the top-of-rack leaf for pc_0_0
  (host subnet 10.0.0.0/24 on eth2). Its only fabric attachment is
  EBGP: neighbor 172.16.0.4 (spine_router_0_0, AS 65100) on eth0 and
  neighbor 172.16.0.8 (spine_router_0_1, AS 65101) on eth1. With bgpd
  dead the leaf stops learning 10.0.1.0/24 and stops advertising
  10.0.0.0/24, so pc_0_0 is isolated from the fabric even though every
  physical link is still UP.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: bgpd not running on leaf_router_0_0
Fix: restart FRR on leaf_router_0_0 (`service frr restart`) -- this lab
  keeps its config in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so a restart fully restores
  the BGP configuration and sessions.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03 on this fabric): bgpd is killed
together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh
remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent
may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is
missing/empty on leaf_router_0_0" -- that is the same fault observed at
the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on leaf_router_0_0. Unlike the vtysh-configured
kath labs, this lab has a persistent /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart
brings bgpd back WITH its full BGP configuration; the sessions to both
spines re-establish and pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 again.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The FRR `bgpd` process (and its supervisor `watchfrr`) on `leaf_router_0_0` has crashed or been killed. The `zebra` daemon is still running, which keeps the two uplink interfaces (`eth0` toward spine_router_0_0 and `eth1` toward spine_router_0_1) in an UP/UP state — exactly what the NOC observed.

**Mechanism:** With `bgpd` dead, `leaf_router_0_0` holds no BGP sessions and cannot advertise its directly-attached prefix `10.0.0.0/24` to either spine. Both spine routers therefore withdraw that prefix from their routing tables and mark the neighbor as `Active` (retrying). Because `leaf_router_0_1` learns `10.0.0.0/24` exclusively via the two spines, it also loses the route, causing it to return "Destination Net Unreachable" to `pc_0_1`. Simultaneously, `leaf_router_0_0`'s own routing table contains only its three connected routes — no path to `10.0.1.0/24` — so it returns "Destination Net Unreachable" to `pc_0_0`. Cross-fabric traffic fails in both directions while intra-subnet (host-to-gateway) pings remain functional.

**Localization:** `leaf_router_0_0` exclusively — all other devices (`leaf_router_0_1`, `spine_router_0_0`, `spine_router_0_1`, `super_spine_router_0`) have their FRR daemons intact and their BGP sessions fully Established.

**Root cause:** The `bgpd` daemon on `leaf_router_0_0` is not running (and `watchfrr` is absent to restart it), eliminating all BGP sessions from that leaf and propagating a routing black-hole across the fabric.

**Fix:** Restart the FRR suite on `leaf_router_0_0` — run `service frr restart` (or `systemctl restart frr`) inside the container. This will bring `watchfrr`, `bgpd`, and related daemons back up, re-establish the two BGP sessions to the spine routers, re-advertise `10.0.0.0/24` fabric-wide, and restore full host-to-host reachability.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies leaf_router_0_0 as the affected device.
The report explicitly states the FRR 'bgpd' process on leaf_router_0_0 is dead/not running (and watchfrr is absent), which satisfies the requirement to identify the BGP daemon being down.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states all other routers (both spines, super-spine, and leaf_router_0_1) have FRR/BGP intact and Established, isolating the fault to leaf_router_0_0.
Recommends restarting the FRR service (service frr restart / systemctl restart frr) on leaf_router_0_0 to bring back bgpd and restore BGP sessions, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log contains direct evidence (ping failures with 'Destination Net Unreachable', bgp_snapshot flagging missing bgpd/watchfrr, pgrep showing only zebra, and kernel routes lacking learned prefixes) that supports its conclusion. The inferences from those observations to 'bgpd not running on leaf_router_0_0' and the recommended FRR restart follow logically and cover the necessary checks to rule out other causes.
